usage.callShape: POST https://utilsforagents.com/v1/image/scrub-metadata — body MUST be raw binary image bytes with Content-Type: image/jpeg or image/png, OR multipart/form-data with field 'file' = the image binary (max 5 MB). NOT JSON, NOT base64.

inputExample._note: no JSON body — send raw image bytes with Content-Type: image/png, or multipart/form-data field 'file' = <binary JPEG/PNG>

usage.outputShape: Response body is the raw cleaned image binary (Content-Type matches the uploaded image format, image/jpeg or image/png) with all EXIF/XMP/IPTC metadata stripped. There is no JSON wrapper — save the response bytes directly as the output image file.
quirks: Binary upload endpoint: requires raw image bytes (Content-Type: image/jpeg|image/png) OR multipart/form-data with field 'file'. Does NOT accept a JSON body or a base64 string.
Output is raw binary image bytes (no JSON envelope); response Content-Type matches the original image format. Save the bytes directly.

COULD NOT TEST via the qa-pay harness: that tool only sends Content-Type application/json, reads --body=@file as utf8 text (corrupting binary), and has no multipart/octet-stream support — so it cannot deliver a valid image to this endpoint. Did not pay (paying would charge $0.003 then 4xx with no usable result). Needs an x402 client that can POST raw binary / multipart file bodies to verify.
Decoded payment-required (x402 v2) confirms input bodyType 'form-data' with required field 'file' and output type 'binary'.
usage.guide: POST the image to https://utilsforagents.com/v1/image/scrub-metadata to strip EXIF/XMP/IPTC metadata. Send the image either as a raw binary body with Content-Type set to image/jpeg or image/png, or as multipart/form-data with a single field named 'file' containing the image bytes (max 5 MB). Pay the $0.003 USDC x402 charge (Base eip155:8453 or Solana). The response body is the cleaned image as raw binary bytes (no JSON) with Content-Type matching the original format — write those bytes straight to a file. Do NOT send a JSON or base64 body; it will be rejected. NOTE: this endpoint was not paid-tested because the QA pay harness cannot send binary/multipart bodies — verify with a binary-capable x402 client before trusting.
